data_quality_notes:
Saturday run, US equities and futures closed. Every equity and ETF figure in this report is the Friday 2026-11-20 official close via finnhub, age ~875 minutes at synthesis — that is a closed market, not a stale quote, and the freshest honest price available. Crypto and the event-contract orderbook were fetched live this morning. Research finished with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block plus a 06:42 addendum, so nothing was truncated.

WHY ONLY FOUR IDEAS, AND ONLY ONE NEW ONE. This is the deliberate output of the tape, not a shortfall of effort. (1) Of eleven instruments levelled, eight closed within 0.7% of their 150-day low after six consecutive down sessions — shorting there is chasing and buying there is a knife-catch. (2) The book already holds 17 open positions, 16 of them long equity/ETF and seven of those defensive, so the correlation cap on the one lane that is working is not merely met but massively exceeded. (3) The one driver with real conviction — 'the correction continues' — is already expressed twice (the IWM short and the Fed-pause contract are the SAME driver, not opposing bets), and the third slot the cap permits was declined on purpose rather than through oversight. Short /MES, short /MNQ, short semis, short XLP and a BTC short were all considered and rejected as worse wrappers on a position already held.

RATIOS WERE RECOMPUTED, NOT TRUSTED. KXFEDDECISION 15/6 = 2.50 (floor 2.0). IWM 31.81/14.00 = 2.27 (floor 2.0). LEN 29.00/11.50 = 2.52 against a stated 68.00 bear case (long_term floor 2.50). None sits suspiciously close to its floor from the target side, and the stop side was checked the other way: IWM's 14.00-point stop is 2.23x its 6.28 ATR14, clearing the 1.8 ATR ETF swing floor. LEN has no stop by design and a bear-case price instead. DKS carries risk_reward null because it is an exit instruction, not an idea — and the REASON for the exit is the ATR test failing: a 129.00 stop sits 0.48 ATR below Friday's close in a name with a 5.15% daily ATR, going into a Monday earnings print. That is a level the stock trades through, not one it stops at.

CHECKS THAT COULD NOT BE RUN. (a) Options-implied moves on every single idea: yahoo-options returned HTTP 401 for IWM and TLT, so the 'is the target inside what the market prices?' test ran on nothing today. No straddle figure is claimed anywhere. (b) No VIX level was fetched and none is stated — yahoo returned 429/401 across the whole run, killing ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^VIX, ^RUT, ^DXY and all ES/NQ/gold/WTI futures quotes; ETF proxies are used throughout and labelled as such. A futures recommendation was therefore impossible to price, which is part of why no /MES, /MNQ or /MBT idea exists. (c) No post-Friday CME FedWatch reading: the 95%/4.3% figures are secondary reports dated 11-16 to 11-19, i.e. PRE-correction. The only post-crash macro read is the Kalshi/Robinhood orderbook itself (pause 8-10c), which is why the Fed idea leans on that rather than on FedWatch. (d) No company fundamentals: no 10-Q, 8-K or transcript was read today, which is why there is no new long_term idea and why the tech-valuation case — the most tempting trade on the board — was rejected rather than published. (e) Not reached at all: FDA calendars, index rebalances, lockup expiries, court dates, small/micro caps (no screener) and short-interest or analyst data on any name.

SOURCES THAT FAILED. yahoo: 429 on all index/futures quotes, 401 on all options chains. finnhub: refused index quotes ('Market data subscription required for CFD indices'), worked for ETFs and single stocks. stooq: 404 on every index symbol. alphavantage: no API key configured. coingecko: the macro subcommand's crypto block failed while the standalone crypto subcommand worked. scripts/market_data.py events is structurally broken rather than facing an unavailable market — it filters one unsorted 200-market Kalshi page client-side, so every topic returns 0 results. Research worked around it via the Kalshi /markets/<ticker>/orderbook endpoint, since /markets returns null for yes_bid/yes_ask/last_price. Worth a fix plus a test: without that workaround the richest lane in today's tape would have been invisible.

TWO ERRORS THE RESEARCH PHASE MADE AND CORRECTED IN PLACE, recorded because the later entry is the one synthesised here. (1) The 06:05 reading of gold -3.67% as a one-day forced liquidation making a dovish pivot more likely was wrong on both counts: GLD is in a 24.8% bear market and the December meeting is 89% priced to HIKE. Anything in the research log before 06:10 that assumes easing is superseded. (2) LEN was first captured as a SWING cancellation with a 95.00 target and a 72.00 stop, all three invented — the published record has it as long_term, entry 79.50, target 108.50, no stop by design. That mattered beyond the numbers, because the cancellation argument attacked a swing premise an idea of this horizon never had. The corrected decision published here slows the accumulation instead of cancelling it.

ONE IDEA CARRIES NO WIN PROBABILITY. LEN's is omitted rather than invented: a long-term accumulation with no stop has no 'target before stop' event to assign a probability to, and the notes support no number. KXFEDDECISION claims 0.36 against a 0.286 break-even (a deliberately modest ~5-point edge over the market's 10c) and IWM claims 0.42 against 0.306.

TRACK-RECORD CONTEXT, which set today's bar rather than decorating it: 45 closed trades, 5 hit target (11%), average -5.8%. Conviction 2 is 0 for 7 at -10.1% average, so no conviction-2 equity long was published today. Stocks are 2/31 at -7.6% against ETFs at 3/14 and -1.9%. PYPL (-5.7%) and ONON (-12.4%) both traded through their stops on Friday and are closed; neither is re-pitched, and no stop on any of the four positions sitting within 3.2% of theirs (XLV, RTX, DKS, HUN) was widened. The value of this report today is in what it closes and trims, not in what it adds.

RED TEAM (phase 2c, separate pass, did not write the above). Cut one of four ideas, corrected a wrong earnings date, and lowered every surviving conviction.

KILLED LEN (was rank 4). It has no stop by design, so its 2.5217:1 reward-to-risk IS its risk control, and that clears the 2.50 long-term floor by 0.02 — on a 108.50 target sitting 13% above the 120-day high of 96.03 with no valuation anchor anywhere in the idea, no fundamental or filing evidence read today (the author says so explicitly), and the only driver actually researched today, the rate path, having moved against it. The ratio admits no legitimate repair: raising the bear case worsens it and moving the target out is the one fix the red team may not make. It also contradicts this report's own claim above that no ratio sits suspiciously close to its floor from the target side — LEN's does, and that claim is withdrawn. The order never filled, so nothing realised is given up; the structural thesis and its business invalidation are kept on the watchlist.

CORRECTED THE DKS EARNINGS DATE, which was the operative fact of rank 3. The print is 2026-11-24 BEFORE THE OPEN (call 08:00 ET) per DICK'S own 2026-11-02 investor-relations release, not 2026-11-23. The fetched finnhub calendar carried 11-23 with a blank hour, and validate_report.py's earnings_date check 'confirmed' it against that same wrong source — a mechanical pass on a bad input. The exit still stands, because a 129.00 stop 0.48 ATR below price in a 5.15%-daily-ATR name cannot survive an earnings gap whichever morning it lands. What changes is the execution: there is no event risk at Monday's open, so the position should be worked out across Monday and flat by its close rather than sold at market into the first minutes of a session that may open as a violent bounce off a 150-day low. The report's outstanding 'may already be post-event' caveat is resolved.

CONVICTIONS LOWERED ON ALL THREE SURVIVORS. KXFEDDECISION 5 -> 3: of its four evidence kinds, 'positioning' is the 8-10c orderbook, which is the price being paid rather than independent evidence that price is wrong (circular), and 'counter_argument_answered' restates the thesis's own AI-capex mechanism from a single strategist quote in a wire story — the same confirmation under a second kind. The one real primary document re-verified clean (FRED GASREGW re-fetched: October weekly average 4.3095 against 3.9843 for November's first three weeks, -7.55%, matching the cited figures to the cent) but it is a HEADLINE energy effect pointed at a committee acting on core, and the report itself concedes the Fed votes with no published statistic containing it. Two genuine confirmations, so conviction 3. IWM 4 -> 3: its 'positioning' evidence argues against its own direction — IWM outperforming SPY by 2.46 points is a reason to cover, which is the action, but not a confirmation of a short. DKS 4 -> 2: a conviction 4 beside direction 'buy' on an idea whose entire content is 'close the position' overstates confidence in the long, and all three of its evidence kinds support exiting.

FIXED, NOT CUT: IWM's stated reason for leaving the stop at 284.50 was wrong. A stop at the 270.50 entry sits 13.89 points from Friday's close, 2.21x the 6.2832 ATR14 and outside the 1.8 ATR ETF floor, so the claim that any meaningful stop 'sits inside 0.5 ATR' does not hold. The conclusion survives on the correct reasoning (measured from the entry, as a filled position must be, any stop under about 281.81 breaches the floor and a breakeven stop would read as infinite reward-to-risk on zero risk), so the forward 0.64:1 is answered by cutting size and not by tightening the stop. Also added to KXFEDDECISION: the November Employment Situation on 2026-12-04 08:30 ET, verified on the BLS calendar, which the idea omitted despite being the largest two-sided event before the vote and the one thing that could supply the labour-market cover key_risk says is missing; and the risk that the December 8-9 meeting carries an SEP, so a Fed worried about financial conditions can hike and signal caution in the dots — the most likely path where this thesis is right and the contract still resolves NO.

NOT CUT, EXPLICITLY. The IWM half-cover and the DKS exit are both sound and both are risk-reducing instructions; the Fed contract is a defensible 1.5% speculative position whose stated 36% win probability is conservative rather than inflated — it implies a fair value near 11.6c against the ~15c the thesis argues for, so it claims less edge than it makes the case for. The FOMC date, its two-day structure and its SEP status were verified against the Federal Reserve's own calendar, and the Nov/Dec CPI and payrolls dates against the BLS calendar. The watchlist was left as written: its rejections (XLK, UUP, the CPI bucket contracts, XLE, GLD, /MBTZ6) are reasoned, numerate and in several cases argue against trades the report would have liked to make, which is the behaviour this phase is meant to reward. Three ideas remain, one of them new.

ONE KNOWN PIPELINE CONSEQUENCE, FLAGGED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND. Because validate_report.py's earnings_date check hard-fails any mismatch against the fetched finnhub calendar, the DKS date correction above will itself trip that check and phase 2d will likely demote DKS to the watchlist citing 'report says 2026-11-24 but the calendar says 2026-11-23'. That demotion reason is wrong — the issuer's own release is the better source — and the exit instruction stands regardless of the rank it ends up with. The red team deliberately did NOT edit the validator to let its own change pass: that check polices precisely this field, a mismatch almost always does mean the model invented a date, and a phase rewriting the logic that audits it is the failure mode this pipeline is built to prevent. The durable fix belongs in tests/ with a human deciding it — a claimed date backed by an issuer citation should warn and rank down, not hard-fail against a third-party calendar whose own hour field was blank. Note also that an exit instruction is advice to the reader and does not itself close the tracked position: the open DKS row keeps being graded against its 129.00 stop and 175.50 target until price reaches one, so the demotion costs prominence, not accuracy. Validation demoted 1 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 2 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

market_context.summary:
Friday 2026-11-20 was a tech-led liquidation that put the Dow and S&P 500 into correction and left the Nasdaq in a bear market. SPY -3.64% to 689.81, closing 4.0% off its own intraday high of 718.29 and on the session low; QQQ -5.67% and XLK -7.27%, a two-sigma sector day. The shape is rotation rather than indiscriminate selling: staples +0.67%, long bonds +1.37% and healthcare -0.12% all held while tech broke. SPY has now fallen six consecutive sessions, 754.37 -> 689.81 = -8.6%, and QQQ sits -20.24% off its high with XLK -26.69%.

The driver named by the reporting is an AI-capex unwind — slowing datacenter buildouts, withdrawn funding for AI projects, a slower tech earnings trajectory. Nvidia fell 13-14% on a Reuters report that the SEC is probing its accounting, and is now -47.5% from its 2026-10-06 peak with roughly $2.7T of market value gone. The Anthropic IPO debuted Friday and closed -8.5% after an initial gain, which is the cleanest available read on sentiment: the marginal buyer for new AI supply has left.

The single most important macro fact, and the one that overturned this run's own opening frame: the Fed is expected to HIKE in December, not cut. The target range is 3.75-4.00%, the last move was a 12-0 quarter-point hike on 2026-09-16, October CPI ran +0.35% m/m, payrolls were +165,000 and unemployment fell to 4.1%. That makes this one discount-rate story rather than three: mega-cap tech -26.7%, gold -24.8% from its high at a 120-day low, and bitcoin 21.9% below the 74,075 level this report wanted to short on 11-09 are all long-duration assets de-rating together, with the haven bid in the DOLLAR (19-month high) rather than in gold or reliably in duration. Banks confirm there is a funding component and not only a multiple one: XLF is -9.11% off its high below both moving averages after five straight down sessions, and KRE sits 0.78% above its 120-day low, which prices credit rather than the net-interest-margin benefit a hiking Fed with a steepening curve should deliver.

The one genuinely new, post-crash macro read is the December FOMC orderbook, fetched live this morning: a 25bp hike at 89-90c, a pause at 8-10c, a 50bp hike at 2-3c, a cut at ~1c. Against pre-Friday FedWatch (95.7% / ~0% / 4.3%) the market has not begun pricing cuts — it has begun pricing a PAUSE and has taken the 50bp tail off the table, which is what a financial-conditions shock landing on hot inflation looks like. Only three instruments on the board are in uptrends: UUP, XLP and TLT. Eight of eleven closed within 0.7% of their 150-day low, so Monday is as likely to be a violent bounce as a continuation — first resistance is SPY 713.56-718.29, QQQ 638.84-643.28, XLK 158.71-159.01, all of them Friday's own range and all well below the SMA20.

catalyst.event: FOMC rate decision, Dec 9 2026 14:00 ET. Contract resolves YES only if the Fed leaves the target range unchanged at 3.75-4.00%. Calendar detail that shapes the trade: the October PCE price index on 2026-11-25 08:30 ET is the LAST major inflation print before the vote — November CPI is not published until 2026-12-10, the day AFTER the decision, and November PCE not until 2026-12-23. Note the 11-25 print covers OCTOBER and therefore predates the November energy collapse. RED TEAM ADDITION: the October PCE print is the last major INFLATION print before the vote, but it is not the last major print. The November Employment Situation lands 2026-12-04 08:30 ET, five days before the decision, verified against the BLS release calendar (November CPI 2026-12-10 confirmed on the same page, i.e. after the vote, as stated). That is the largest two-sided event between here and resolution, and it is the one that can change the specific thing key_risk says is missing — labour-market cover for a pause. The FOMC meeting is confirmed as 2026-12-08/09 on the Federal Reserve's own calendar and carries a Summary of Economic Projections.
catalyst.action: Buy YES at 10c or better, up to 12c, sized as a speculative position. This is a repricing trade, not a hold-to-resolution bet. The near catalyst is the 2026-11-25 08:30 ET October PCE print, four sessions away and two-sided — but do not expect it to carry the November disinflation, because it covers October. What takes this contract to 20-30c is a still-falling tape into early December, or any FOMC voter publicly floating a wait; that is where to scale out. A firm PCE print alongside stabilising equities is the signal to cut, not to average down. Hold a residual to Dec 9 only with the scale-out money banked. Do not add above 12c and do not average down below 6c. The 2026-12-04 08:30 ET November payrolls print is the event to trade this around: a materially weak print is the most likely route from 10c to 25c, and a firm one alongside stabilising equities is the cut signal.

recommendations.thesis: The market prices a 10% chance the Fed leaves rates unchanged on Dec 9. The claim is that this is too low by a few points, on two things the price looks to be underweighting. First, the thing breaking is itself disinflationary: the selloff is an AI-capex unwind — slowing datacenter buildouts and withdrawn funding for AI projects — a negative investment shock to exactly the industrial, power and labour demand that kept core inflation sticky. Second, and this is verifiable rather than narrative, the disinflation is already arriving through energy: US regular gasoline averaged $4.309 in October and $3.984 across the first three weeks of November, -7.55% and still falling, worth roughly -0.3pp on the November CPI index at its basket weight. Layered on that, financial conditions tightened violently and the move is young — the S&P and Dow entered correction only on Friday, the Nasdaq is 20.2% off its high, and roughly $4 trillion of market value went in five sessions. The pricing itself shows how fast this re-rates: the pause went from essentially nothing pre-Friday to 8-10c in one session while the 50bp tail was cut from 4.3% to 2-3%. The market is already moving this way and has 12 more sessions to do it in.
recommendations.key_risk: The base case is firmly a hike and this contract loses in it. October CPI ran +0.35% m/m, the October minutes had almost all officials seeing further increases as appropriate, the September hike was 12-0 with no dissent, and payrolls were +165,000 with unemployment at 4.1% and falling, so there is no labour-market cover for a pause. The sharpest specific risk is one of sequencing, and it cuts against this trade: the Fed votes on Dec 9 having seen NO official data containing the November energy drop — November CPI lands 12-10, the day after, and November PCE on 12-23. The 11-25 print covers October and may even read firm. So the cleanest argument for waiting is one the committee cannot yet point to in a published statistic, and pausing would read as subordinating the inflation mandate to equity prices with the 10-year at 5.04%. Event-contract specifics matter enormously at a 10c entry: Robinhood's panel showed $0.00 but the disclosure says additional fees apply and the product launched at 2c per contract, so a 1-2c round trip moves break-even from 10% to 11-12% — verify the fill cost before sizing. Finally, 10c is not a claim of Fed autopilot; the price already embeds part of this scenario, so the edge asserted is about 5 points, not a repricing to a coin flip. RED TEAM ADDITION — the dovish outcome has a cheaper expression than the one this contract pays on. The December 8-9 meeting carries a Summary of Economic Projections (confirmed on the Fed's own calendar), so a committee that has become worried about financial conditions can hike 25bp and signal caution in the dots and the press conference instead of pausing. That is the single most likely way this thesis is directionally RIGHT and the contract still resolves NO, and it is an argument for taking the 25c scale-out rather than holding to resolution. Second, the disinflation evidence is pointed at the wrong index: the gasoline move is verified (-7.55% m/m, FRED GASREGW, re-fetched and matching to the cent) but it is a HEADLINE energy effect, while the committee that hiked 12-0 and wrote that further increases were appropriate is acting on core. Energy at -7.55% does not move core, so the strongest piece of primary evidence here supports a weaker claim than the thesis draws from it.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against: a Fed that has hiked into re-accelerating inflation, unanimously, and told the world in its own minutes that more is coming does not stop because the Nasdaq gave back a year of gains, particularly when unemployment is falling. Equity corrections did not stop hiking cycles in 1994 or 2022 when inflation was the problem. Answered rather than waved away: this trade does not need the Fed to pause. It needs the probability of a pause to be re-rated once, by a tape that already moved it from nothing to 10c in one session, and the exit is 25c rather than resolution for exactly that reason. The honest residual is that if equities simply stabilise over the next fortnight, the contract decays to 4c and the trade is a loss.
